body:
What UNESCO inscribed in 2023

Garba of Gujarat was inscribed in 2023 on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. It is an important Gujarat-specific entry in India's UNESCO intangible heritage record.

Garba is a ritual and devotional dance tradition especially associated with the festival of Navaratri. It centres on collective participation, music, movement and the celebration of feminine divine energy, traditionally represented through a ceremonial lamp or associated sacred imagery.

UNESCO's recognition concerns the living cultural practice and its transmission by communities. It does not refer to the inscription of a single dance ground, festival venue, musical instrument or physical monument.

Why Garba is intangible cultural heritage

A living tradition remains part of cultural heritage when people continue to practise it, recognise its meaning and pass it on. Garba is learned and sustained through families, communities, local celebrations and organised cultural activities. Participants, musicians, artisans and other community members contribute to the continuity of the tradition.

This explains why safeguarding intangible heritage is different from simply repairing a monument. The tradition must remain meaningful and capable of being transmitted to future generations.

Safeguarding can include documentation, awareness, education and support for the communities that maintain the practice. UNESCO inscription can increase visibility, but the existence of a list entry does not replace the participation of the people who keep the tradition alive.

Garba, Rani-ki-Vav and Gujarat's other traditions

Gujarat possesses many historically important cultural practices and objects. However, not every well-known tradition is separately inscribed by UNESCO.

ExampleNature of heritageUNESCO status on 23 November 2026
Garba of GujaratLiving dance and festive traditionIntangible Representative List, 2023
Rani-ki-Vav, PatanHistoric architectural stepwellWorld Heritage List, 2014
Patola of PatanTraditional textile and weaving craftNot separately inscribed on India's intangible Representative List
BandhaniTraditional tie-dye textile craftNot separately inscribed on India's intangible Representative List
Bhavai of GujaratTraditional folk theatreNot separately inscribed on India's intangible Representative List

Patola is closely associated with Patan, while Bandhani is a widespread textile tradition with important centres in Gujarat, including Kutch and Saurashtra. Bhavai is an important Gujarati folk-theatre tradition. Their cultural significance does not depend on their separate inclusion in UNESCO's list.

Garba and Deepavali are different UNESCO entries

Garba of Gujarat was inscribed in 2023 as a tradition associated particularly with Gujarat and Navaratri. Deepavali was inscribed in 2025 as a festival celebrated across India.

Both belong to intangible cultural heritage, but their names, years and cultural associations differ. Deepavali's inclusion does not change Garba's earlier inscription year.

Prelims focus

  • Garba of Gujarat: Inscribed in 2023.
  • List: Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
  • Festival association: Navaratri.
  • Heritage type: Living ritual and dance tradition.
  • Deepavali: Separate intangible heritage inscription in 2025.
  • Trap: Patola, Bandhani and Bhavai are not separately inscribed elements on India's Representative List at the stated cutoff.

[UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Garba of Gujarat, element 01962, inscription decision 18.COM 8.b.32, 2023; UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, India, Elements on the Lists, including Deepavali, 2025; Sangeet Natak Akademi, Intangible Cultural Heritage, Garba of Gujarat; NCERT, Living Craft Traditions of India, Class XI, chapter Crafts Heritage, printed pp. 9–12, Gujarat textiles and craft traditions. UNESCO records consulted 23 November 2026.]

title: Garba of Gujarat: UNESCO Recognition and the Safeguarding of Living Heritage

body:
International recognition and national conservation are different functions

UNESCO, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH) are all associated with heritage, but they have different legal identities and responsibilities.

UNESCO provides international conventions and frameworks for heritage recognition and cooperation. ASI is a government archaeological organisation responsible for the protection and conservation of centrally protected monuments and archaeological sites. INTACH is an independent heritage organisation that works on awareness, documentation and conservation.

UNESCO and the World Heritage Committee

UNESCO is a specialised agency of the United Nations. The World Heritage system operates under the 1972 Convention. The World Heritage Committee, an intergovernmental body established under that Convention, makes inscription decisions for the World Heritage List.

The World Heritage Centre serves the Convention's work and coordinates processes such as receiving nominations and supporting the Committee. Expert organisations such as ICOMOS and IUCN advise on the cultural and natural significance of proposed properties.

UNESCO inscription does not transfer ownership of an Indian monument to UNESCO. Responsibility for protecting and managing the property remains with India and the relevant authorities under applicable laws and arrangements.

Archaeological Survey of India

The Archaeological Survey of India was established in 1861. Alexander Cunningham was appointed the first Archaeological Surveyor in December 1861. ASI functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.

An important legal framework for ASI's work is the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. Under the Act, ancient monuments and archaeological sites may be declared to be of national importance. ASI undertakes their protection, maintenance and archaeological conservation.

ASI's work includes monuments such as temples, forts, caves, tombs and other archaeological remains. It also undertakes archaeological investigations, documentation and conservation activities.

Not every historically important monument in India is necessarily under ASI. Some monuments are protected by state governments under state laws, while others may be managed through different public, private, religious or local arrangements.

ASI protection and UNESCO inscription are separate statuses. A monument may be centrally protected under Indian law without being on the World Heritage List. Conversely, UNESCO recognition does not itself replace the country's legal system of monument protection.

Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage

INTACH stands for the Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage. It was founded in 1984 and established as a registered society.

INTACH works through heritage specialists, programmes and regional chapters. Its activities include identifying and documenting heritage, supporting conservation, promoting public awareness, heritage education and efforts relating to built, natural and intangible heritage.

Unlike ASI, INTACH is not a department of the Government of India and does not possess the same statutory authority over centrally protected monuments. Unlike the World Heritage Committee, it cannot itself inscribe a property on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

Comparison of the three institutions

InstitutionNatureMain heritage role
UNESCO and its heritage committeesInternational organisation and convention-based bodiesInternational recognition, standards, safeguarding and cooperation
ASIGovernment of India archaeological organisationArchaeology, conservation and protection of centrally protected monuments and sites
INTACHIndependent registered heritage societyHeritage documentation, awareness, education and conservation initiatives

Applying the distinction

For a question asking who decides the inscription of a cultural property, the correct institution is the World Heritage Committee, informed by expert evaluation. For a question asking about the conservation of a centrally protected archaeological monument in India, ASI is the relevant government organisation. For a question about an independent heritage society established in 1984, the answer is INTACH.

The same distinction applies in Gujarat. The international significance of Rani-ki-Vav is recognised through its World Heritage inscription, while its conservation takes place through Indian institutions and legal arrangements. Garba's inscription belongs to the separate intangible heritage system and depends on the continuation of a living community tradition.

One-glance revision of the complete topic

At the 23 November 2026 cutoff, India's heritage records show 45 World Heritage properties under the 1972 system and 16 inscribed intangible heritage elements under the 2003 system. Gujarat has 4 inscribed cultural World Heritage properties and the UNESCO-listed intangible element Garba of Gujarat.

Prelims focus

  • ASI: Established in 1861; first Archaeological Surveyor Alexander Cunningham.
  • ASI's principal monument-protection framework: Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958.
  • INTACH: Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage, established in 1984.
  • ICOMOS: Cultural World Heritage evaluation; IUCN: Natural World Heritage evaluation.
  • World Heritage Committee: Decides World Heritage inscriptions.
  • Trap: UNESCO recognition, ASI statutory protection and INTACH conservation activities are not interchangeable.

[UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 1972 World Heritage Convention, Articles 4 and 8–11; World Heritage List Nominations, Advisory Bodies and Committee examination; Archaeological Survey of India, History, section From 1861 to 1901; ASI, Monuments and Conservation and Preservation, provisions of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958; INTACH, About INTACH and INTACH History, establishment in 1984; UNESCO World Heritage Centre, India State Party profile; UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, India, Elements on the Lists. Online sources consulted 23 November 2026.]

title: UNESCO, ASI and INTACH: Who Recognises, Protects and Conserves Heritage?
